messages:
support-jen: FYI getting multiple escalations from a few customers in eu-west2: intermittent 502s on /v1/generate, spikes of latency, a couple of users also reported 401s after a retry. customers report duplicate billing for the same request when they retried. :rotating_light:
customer-alex (ACME): we saw ~20% of calls fail with 502s for ~15m, then a retry succeeded but we were billed twice — this breaks our billing reconciliation. ticket #INC-4219 attached.
maya (oncall): thanks Jen. can you paste a minimal repro from the customer and sample headers? also @netops-lin please check any regional network telemetry for eu-west2.
support-jen: pasted their curl repro below (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  -d '{"input":"short prompt"}' -v

*Attempt1* -> TCP RST / 502 from gateway
*Attempt2* -> 200 OK, generation returned
```
customer-alex (ACME): exact response from our side looked like:
```
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Connection: close

{"error":"upstream read timeout"}
```
then retry -> 200. we use no idempotency keys on our side so retry = duplicate bill.
sre-ash: I'm seeing elevated 5xx rate for eu-west2-hosted inference gateway starting ~1938887800, peaked ~1938888800. Correlating with network drops on the host NICs. grabbing tcpdump now.
netops-lin: I can see increased retransmits & a few RX errors on the host vNICs in eu-west2-az3. also noticed a flurry of BGP updates from transit provider X around the same time — possible microlooping causing packet re-order/retransmit. pulling BGP session logs.
infra-bot: deploy-detect: no recent gateway config deploys to eu-west2 in last 6h.
netops-lin: traceroute from gateway host to model serving fleet (shortened):
```
traceroute to model-node-12 (10.4.12.8), 30 hops max
 1  10.0.0.1  0.49 ms
 2  172.16.2.5  1.2 ms
 3  * * *  
 4  203.0.113.1  12.4 ms  (provider peering)
 5  198.51.100.7  30.2 ms  AS64500  (flapping)
 6  10.4.12.8  31.0 ms
```
netops-lin: tcpdump snippet shows repeated retransmits and some dup acks:
```
15:12:03.123456 IP gw->model  Flags [P.], seq 345:789, ack 901, win 65535
15:12:03.124012 IP gw->model  Flags [P.], seq 345:789  (retransmission)
15:12:03.124500 IP model->gw  Flags [.], ack 789, dup-ack
```
samir (eng-runtime): that pattern matches intermittent packet loss causing the gateway to not receive upstream chunked responses in time -> gateway returns 502. runtime should tolerate some reordering but not loss at this rate. we have a CV in request-retry logic: if gateway gets TCP RST or read timeout it retries upstream without idempotency handling at the billing layer — that can cause double billing.
maya (oncall): mitigation plan:
- net ops: open ticket with transit provider X and request immediate mitigation / announce we will shift egress.
- infra: fail traffic from eu-west2-az3 to eu-west2-az1 (cross-az) and enable regional reroute to eu-west1 for critical customers.
- eng-runtime: apply hotfix to gateway to treat upstream read-timeouts as 503 (retry-safe) and ensure billing dedupe for immediate window OR disable auto-retry on the gateway for non-idempotent calls.
- billing: pause charge for affected requests window and create refund batch for customers who report duplicates.
netops-lin: provider says they saw a short-lived BGP churn at 15:10 UTC, they rolled a config to stop the noise but we should still shift traffic away from their peering for the next hour. initiating route preference change now.
sre-ash: toggling cross-az egress to avoid the problematic path. impact: small increase in p95 latency (~40ms) but should remove retransmit spikes. toggling now.
infra-bot: route-update: origin-pref changed for eu-west2 egress -> success.
support-jen: letting affected customers know we're routing around provider and investigating billing. Can we get an ETA on when refunds will be issued?
billing-kim: creating refund run for all confirmed duplicate-charge customers between 1938887000-1938889200. ETA: 24-48h for initial refunds, will expedite for enterprise accounts. tagging finance for audit.
samir (eng-runtime): rolling a small gateway hotfix to change retry behavior and emit an explicit idempotency-missing header for diagnostics. pushing canary to eu-west1, then eu-west2 (non-az3 hosts first).
sre-ash: monitoring 5xx rate. early signs: 5xx dropped ~70% after reroute. still seeing scattered 502s from older hosts that still used the old egress.
maya (oncall): for support replies: advise customers to set an idempotency key header (Idempotency-Key) on non-idempotent POSTs as a short-term workaround and we'll refund duplicates. also escalate any enterprise SLA breaches to sales ops.
customer-alex (ACME): thanks — appreciate the quick action. can you confirm we will get a refund for the duplicate charge and the timeframe?
billing-kim: confirmed — you will be included in the refund batch, reference INC-4219.
sre-ash: follow-up action items:
- netops: confirm provider baseline stability and request RFO from provider X (owner: netops-lin)
- eng-runtime: postmortem on retry/billing coupling and implement server-side idempotency dedupe at billing gateway (owner: samir)
- infra: add egress health checks to detect retransmit spikes and automatically shift preference (owner: infra-team)
- support: notify impacted customers + collect any missing cases (owner: support-jen)
- billing: complete refund batch and provide ledger entries (owner: billing-kim)
maya (oncall): assigning postmortem owner: @sre-ash. please own timeline and runbook updates. I'll update incident channel and mark as sev2 for now, downgraded from sev1 because routing mitigations worked.
support-jen: sending update to customers now with workaround (Idempotency-Key) and expected refund window.
customer-alex (ACME): all good — please keep us updated if anything else is needed.
infra-bot: incident-closure-suggest: no, still monitoring (next check in 30m).
